bbc.description: The former Murdoch media executive was overheard at an event referring to the way Grace Tame was dressed.

bbc.description: Erin Patterson is serving life in prison for poisoning her relatives with a toxic mushroom lunch in 2023.

bbc.title: Clashes mar European games as Macron condemns violence
bbc.description: Violent clashes mar a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.

bbc.title: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
bbc.description: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia has not.

bbc.title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
bbc.description: The endangered reptiles were bound with duct tape to prevent them moving, officials say.

bbc.title: Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
bbc.description: The legislation has been criticised for enabling political persecution since it was introduced two years ago.

bbc.title: EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
bbc.description: Aid for Ukraine was among the disputes as EU members hope to conclude talks by the end of the year.

bbc.title: Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years over pregnant girlfriend's murder
bbc.description: The pregnant student was murdered after leaving a hotel with a journalist she had contacted to discuss her affair with the governor.

bbc.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row
bbc.description: The Ugandan army is helping the Congolese military fight an Islamist militant group in the east of the country.

bbc.title: Guinea-Bissau's military leaders delay return to civilian rule until 2028
bbc.description: The announcement comes a year after a military coup with its leaders promising a return to civilian rule within 12 months.

bbc.title: Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65
bbc.description: Simon Le Bon and his other bandmates say Taylor "brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music".

bbc.title: Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
bbc.description: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as officials urged residents to leave the area.

bbc.title: Politics and peek-a-boo in Australian parliament as senator brings baby to work
bbc.description: Senator Lidia Thorpe kept 6-month-old Aaliyah entertained, as her mum Senator Fatima Payman, participated in an online safety bill debate.

bbc.title: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
bbc.description: Hundreds of thousands have been affected by storms in the country as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend begins.

rfi.title: UN marks first global day against child marriage as millions remain at risk
rfi.description: Friday marks the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, created by the United Nations to spotlight a practice that affects hundreds of millions of women and girls across the globe.

rfi.title: Mali remains strategic for Russia despite heavy losses, investigator says
rfi.description: Russia is unlikely to pull out of Mali despite losing more than 10 percent of its forces there, an investigator who tracks Russian military deployments told RFI. Lou Osbourn co-founded All Eyes On Wagner, a collective of journalists and cybersecurity analysts. She said the losses prove that Russian fighters are taking part in operations alongside Malian troops and that "Africa remains an area of interest for Moscow".

rfi.title: EU budget decision pushed back as leaders fail to bridge divides
rfi.description: A European Union summit failed to bridge deep divides over the bloc's 2028-2034 budget, ending without an agreement after some members walked out. With negotiations due to resume in December, the pressure is on to reach a solution before France and other countries head into a key election year.

rfi.title: French citizens tasked with finding solutions to country's debt crisis
rfi.description: France on Friday launches a citizens' convention on public finances, bringing together 150 randomly selected French people representative of the population to debate how the country can reduce its ballooning deficit and regain control of its finances.

rfi.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over 'links to terrorist acts'
rfi.description: Costa Rica's government said Thursday it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".

rfi.title: Five countries bordering Russia withdraw from global landmine ban treaty
rfi.description: Five European countries have withdrawn from the international treaty banning anti-personnel landmines over security fears linked to Russia, with two preparing to reintroduce the weapons, a report by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines and the Cluster Munition Coalition has said.

rfi.title: French woman on trial for Islamic State propaganda says she is 'ashamed'
rfi.description: The trial of one of France’s most notorious female jihadists opened in Paris on Thursday. Accused of becoming one of the Islamic State group’s most active French propagandists after travelling to Syria in 2012, Émilie König said she was "ashamed" and apologised to the French nation.

rfi.title: Iraq sentences eight French Islamic State members to life as prosecutions continue
rfi.description: Iraq has sentenced eight more French men to life in prison for joining the so-called Islamic State armed group. They are among 47 French citizens transferred to Iraq from neighbouring Syria last year for prosecution.

rfi.title: French media reveal more anti-Semitic messages allegedly sent by Jordan Bardella
rfi.description: French media on Thursday revealed what was described as new evidence that the president of the far-right National Rally party, Jordan Bardella, wrote anti-Semitic messages over Facebook as a teenager. Two months after investigative site Mediapart first revealed conspiracist remarks about Jewish people allegedly sent by Bardella, the outlet and newspaper Le Monde published extracts from a 2013 conversation which they said contained further anti-Semitic comments.

rfi.title: EU rejects new US tariffs targeting industrial overcapacity
rfi.description: The European Union has rejected the rationale behind new tariffs proposed by the United States on several trading partners, to fight what Washington describes as excess industrial capacity, and said it expects the US to honour its existing trade deal with the bloc.

rfi.title: Shredder-wielding Cannes mayor surges into French presidential race
rfi.description: A little-known mayor whom supporters liken to the French version of Argentina's chainsaw-wielding president Javier Milei has been catapulted into third place in France's polarised presidential race, shooting up the polls five months before the vote.

rfi.title: Romans burn PSG's perfect start to Champions League campaign
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain's flawless start to the defence of their Champions League crown ended on Wednesday night in a 2-2 draw with Roma.

rfi.title: EU plans €50bn tech fund to compete with US and China in the quantum race
rfi.description: The European Union on Wednesday announced plans for a fund of up to €50 billion to boost artificial intelligence and quantum computing, alongside new rules favouring EU companies for public contracts. The bloc aims to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 and avoid losing further ground to the United States and China.

rfi.title: French FM defends Ukraine's attacks on Russian ships in Libya
rfi.description: France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Wednesday that Ukraine had been exercising its "absolute right to self-defence" by attacking two Russian ships in Libyan waters.

rfi.title: Moroccan football federation vows to continue legal fight over 2025 AFCON win
rfi.description: The Royal Moroccan Football Federation was on Wednesday preparing a new legal fight after the Court of Arbitration for Sport restored the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title to Senegal.

rfi.title: Israel accused of preventing births in Gaza as Amnesty seeks genocide probe
rfi.description: Israeli measures have prevented births in Gaza, Amnesty International said on Wednesday – calling for the International Criminal Court to investigate whether they amount to an act of genocide. In a report documenting the war’s devastating toll on women and girls, the rights group detailed the collapse of fertility services and deadly shortages of medicines needed during childbirth.

rfi.title: Women in France face financial hurdles to escaping domestic abuse, report finds
rfi.description: Money can be one of the biggest barriers to escaping domestic violence for women around the world. In France, leaving an abusive partner can cost a woman up to 11 months' salary in the first three months alone, a report published on Wednesday has found. Its authors are calling for greater public support, warning that the expense can prevent women from leaving or force some to return to violent partners.

rfi.title: France urged to put women's safety at heart of migration policies
rfi.description: France's High Council for Equality between Women and Men is calling for gender to be a "central aspect" of migration policies, warning that the violence migrant women suffer throughout their journeys is being ignored. The call comes as the world marks International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on Wednesday.

euronews.title: A green valley with a circular twist: Austria´s  shapes the sustainable tech of tomorrow
euronews.description: Austria´s Green Tech Valley Cluster hosts 300 companies — including 20 global tech leaders — shaping the innovative and circular technologies of the future. They are developing solutions in sectors like hydropower, solar thermal, wind, recycling, batteries or electro-mobility — all made in Europe.

euronews.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan reopen key border crossing for up to 100,000 travellers a day
euronews.description: The reopening comes as the EU seeks stronger transport and trade links with Central Asia. The upgraded checkpoint could also ease pressure on regional freight routes and support cross-border tourism.

euronews.title: EU budget summit collapses as row over money exposes clash over Europe's strategic tasks
euronews.description: The EU summit on the Union's common budget for 2028-2034 has initially failed. Some want to protect established spending, others to cut costs and mainly finance new strategic tasks, warns foreign policy expert Alexander Wolf of the Hanns Seidel Foundation in Berlin.

euronews.title: ‘Live and ongoing’ cyber incident takes down UK Department for Work and Pensions online services
euronews.description: The UK government department took the decision to take down the services as a precaution after it detected a cyber incident affecting its systems.

euronews.title: Meet Eba, the 11-year-old poop-sniffing dog helping to protect endangered orcas
euronews.description: Unlike most pooches, Eba spends her days on a boat - assisting scientists in the fight to save dwindling killer whale populations.

euronews.title: North Korea halts Russia military aid over Seoul row, Kyiv says
euronews.description: Ukraine's military intelligence said Kim Jong-un personally ordered the suspension after Russia's deputy foreign minister said it would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.

euronews.title: No burqas at school and fewer foreign pupils: Italy passes controversial education law
euronews.description: The school decree, which includes new rules on digital transition, was finally approved in the Chamber on Thursday. During the vote, opposition MPs displayed signs saying "At school no one is a foreigner".

euronews.title: France's government faces mounting pressure from both sides of the barricades
euronews.description: Exhausted by weeks of street protests, French police officers are demanding better pay, more resources and greater protection. Meanwhile, students and trade unions are determined to maintain their mobilisation, despite what they deem as a strategy of repression aimed at stifling the movement.

euronews.title: EU budget row: Macron accuses Le Pen of 'strange arrogance'
euronews.description: The RN presidential candidate accuses the European Commission of seeking to "rush" adoption of the next EU budget before the 2027 French election.

euronews.title: Son of Myanmar's Suu Kyi 'relieved' by first call in five years, questions military's motives
euronews.description: Speaking to Euronews’ The World Conversation, Kim Aris described his relief at hearing his mother’s voice after five years, called for tougher sanctions enforcement and defended her record on the Rohingya genocide ruling.

euronews.title: Video captures king tide sweeping man and dog into the sea
euronews.description: A man and his dog were swept into the surf by a powerful incoming wave at Cannon Beach, Oregon, after he had earlier been warned by police about the dangers of King Tides. Both managed to escape the water without injury.

euronews.title: A travel guide to Ljubljana – a 2027 European Capital of Tourism
euronews.description: Named one of the European Capitals of Tourism for 2027, Ljubljana offers travellers riverside cafés, historic landmarks and traditional cuisine. Here’s why you should visit the Slovenian capital.

euronews.title: Portugal's parliament orders public TV to air bullfights again, sparking 86,000-name petition
euronews.description: After six years away, bullfights are set to return to RTP programming in 2027, via a Chega proposal, sparking controversy and a petition with over 86,000 signatures.

euronews.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' - Fincher with fries?
euronews.description: Nostalgia and nihilism collide in David Fincher's gritty but edgeless follow-up to Quentin Tarantino's 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood'.

euronews.title: Marseille stadium violence escalates into diplomatic affair between France and Bulgaria
euronews.description: Clashes between Marseille and Bulgarian fans broke out on Thursday evening before the Europa League match OM–Levski Sofia; eleven Bulgarians were injured, five hospitalised.

euronews.title: Does Europe have a cybersecurity problem? | Password
euronews.description: According to experts, the cybersecurity incidents Europe experienced in November should not come as a surprise. But how much do we know about these attacks? And what can Europe do to improve its cybersecurity?

euronews.title: Feijóo vows to quit if he loses Spanish election and dares Sánchez to do the same
euronews.description: Feijóo dared Sánchez to give up his seat and his legal protection if he loses. The prime minister declined.

euronews.title: Spain’s conservative and far-right parties likely to ‘secure a majority’ in Sunday’s election, expert says
euronews.description: Javier Martínez-Cantó, political scientist at the Institute of Public Goods and Policies (IPP–CSIC), believes corruption scandals "have been hindering the popularity" of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez as he tries to stay in power ahead of Sunday's snap elections.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Marine Le Pen veut contraindre les journalistes à respecter le secret de l’instruction
lemonde.description: Interrogée par notre journaliste politique Corentin Lesueur, spécialiste de l’extrême droite, lors d’un point presse, Marine Le Pen a déclaré : « Les médias ne pourront plus en toute impunité effectuer des recels de violation du secret de l’enquête et de l’instruction ».

lemonde.title: « On paie 15 000 euros l’année pour que l’école fasse faillite ? » : des étudiants en colère et en galère après la fermeture de leur école de commerce
lemonde.description: Redressements judiciaires, rachats, disparitions… Après avoir longtemps surfé sur la vague de l’apprentissage, de nombreuses business schools privées se retrouvent en difficulté. Pour leurs élèves, c’est le début d’un parcours du combattant, entre interlocuteurs injoignables, diplôme incertain, nouvelle école à trouver et argent perdu.

lemonde.title: Ecrits antisémites de Jordan Bardella : Marine Le Pen renouvelle sa confiance au président du Rassemblement national
lemonde.description: Le président du RN réitère sa défense en contestant « formellement » les nouvelles révélations du « Monde » et de « Mediapart », se refusant de nouveau à avancer des éléments.

lemonde.title: OM - Levski Sofia : l’Olympique de Marseille menacé de lourdes sanctions par l’UEFA après les violences lors du match de Ligue Europa
lemonde.description: Au lendemain des heurts survenus dans le stade, qui ont fait 11 blessés parmi les supporteurs bulgares, le parquet de Marseille a annoncé l’ouverture de deux enquêtes. L’OM, quant à lui, s’attend à l’ouverture d’une procédure disciplinaire de l’UEFA.

lemonde.title: « C’est presque aussi facile d’acheter un sac Balenciaga qu’un paquet de nouilles de riz » : les articles de luxe d’occasion à Shanghaï bousculent le marché
lemonde.description: Dans des magasins aussi grands que des supermarchés, les plateformes chinoises de revente attirent de jeunes clients qui, sur fond de crise de la consommation, ne veulent plus payer les prix exorbitants pratiqués par les grandes maisons.

lemonde.title: Jean-Claude Vannier, arrangeur indissociable de Serge Gainsbourg et père de l’album-concept « Histoire de Melody Nelson », est mort à l’âge de 83 ans
lemonde.description: Le binôme de Serge Gainsbourg lors de la création de l’album « Histoire de Melody Nelson », est mort jeudi. Pianiste, arrangeur mais encore auteur autodidacte, il avait orchestré les morceaux de nombreuses stars de la chanson française.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Russie a ciblé des infrastructures civiles et énergétiques dans neuf oblasts pendant la nuit, déplore le premier ministre ukrainien
lemonde.description: Dans l’oblast de Dnipropetrovsk – où une personne a été tuée par les attaques –, Moscou a bombardé les gares de Kryvy Rih et de Kamianske, ainsi que deux mines de charbon, et endommagé des locomotives. Le ministère de la défense russe a aussi dit avoir touché une sous-station électrique de la ville Kryvy Rih.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann cherche à tisser un réseau d’élus locaux
lemonde.description: Lors de rencontres au Salon des maires à Paris, puis en Mayenne jeudi, le candidat de Place publique et du Parti socialiste multiplie les appels aux élus de gauche à s’investir dans la campagne. Il promet de faire de son « conseil des territoires » un pilier de sa gouvernance.

lemonde.title: Les subtiles oscillations de David Lisnard, du vote Macron à la main tendue au RN
lemonde.description: Le candidat de droite à la présidentielle rejette dos à dos Emmanuel Macron et Marine Le Pen. Par le passé, sans jamais les soutenir, le maire de Cannes a parfois été plus conciliant, votant pour l’un en 2017, courtisant l’autre en 2025.

lemonde.title: Manifestations du 28 novembre : les marchés de Noël « constituent une vulnérabilité supplémentaire », dit le ministre Laurent Nuñez
lemonde.description: « Cette journée comportera le risque de voir plusieurs cortèges non autorisés se former, dans le but de rechercher l’affrontement avec les forces de l’ordre », a affirmé le ministre de l’intérieur dans un télégramme adressé aux préfets et aux responsables de sécurité.

lemonde.title: Louis Degos, bâtonnier de Paris : « L’Etat a oublié un principe essentiel de droit : la juste mesure »
lemonde.description: Le représentant élu des avocats parisiens lance un appel au respect de l’Etat de droit, remis en cause, selon lui, autant par l’Etat face aux manifestations que dans les propositions de nombreux candidats à l’élection présidentielle.

lemonde.title: Elections législatives en Espagne : la gauche régionaliste espère avancer ses pions
lemonde.description: Plusieurs formations radicales, régionalistes ou indépendantistes, pourraient voir le nombre de leurs députés augmenter significativement. Concurrentes de Podemos et du Frente Amplio, qui ont gouverné ces dernières années avec les socialistes, elles pourraient bouleverser le paysage de la gauche espagnole.

lemonde.title: José Beaurain, député RN de l’Aisne, visé par une enquête pour « détournement de fonds publics » et contesté localement
lemonde.description: Après les révélations du « Canard enchaîné » et l’ouverture d’une enquête préliminaire, le député d’extrême droite, réinvesti par le Rassemblement national malgré des alertes internes, sera l’objet d’une mobilisation à Chauny, samedi.

lemonde.title: Est-ce utile de nourrir les oiseaux l’hiver ?
lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, l’équipe du podcast Chaleur humaine répond à vos questions sur la transition climatique

lemonde.title: Tempêtes aux Etats-Unis : plus de 900 000 foyers sans électricité sur la Côte est le jour de Thanksgiving
lemonde.description: De fortes pluies, du vent violent et des inondations côtières ont affecté l’est du pays en ce jour férié aux Etats-Unis.

lemonde.title: Radio France demande des sanctions alourdies pour les auteurs de violences contre des journalistes
lemonde.description: La PDG du groupe public, Sibyle Veil, plaide pour que le code pénal prévoit que l’agression d’un journaliste constitue une « circonstance aggravante ». France Télévisions et BFM-TV annoncent au « Monde » soutenir la proposition.

france24fr.title: Échanges de coups, jets de projectiles, saluts nazis : soirée chaotique à Marseille contre le Levski
france24fr.description:
Des affrontements ont éclaté avant le coup d'envoi du match OM-Levski Sofia, ce jeudi 26 novembre, au stade Vélodrome de Marseille.
 
Des jets de projectiles ont entouré la zone visiteurs, tandis que des saluts nazis et des imitations de singes à l'encontre des supporters marseillais ont été filmés. 
 
Ces violences ont fait réagir jusqu'aux présidences française et bulgare.

france24fr.title: Marine Le Pen soutient Bardella et veut obliger les journalistes à respecter le secret des enquêtes
france24fr.description: Vendredi, Marine Le Pen a réitéré sa confiance en Jordan Bardella après la publication de nouveaux éléments lui attribuant des écrits antisémites durant sa jeunesse. Dans la même interview, la candidate du Rassemblement national à l’élection présidentielle a annoncé qu'elle obligerait les journalistes à respecter le secret de l'instruction si elle est élue.

france24fr.title: Incidents et blessés à Marseille lors d'OM-Levski Sofia : ce que l'on sait
france24fr.description: De violents affrontements ont éclaté jeudi 26 novembre 2026 au stade Vélodrome avant le match de Ligue Europa entre l'OM et le Levski Sofia (victoire marseillaise 1-0), faisant au moins 11 blessés côté bulgare et provoquant de vives réactions diplomatiques entre la France et la Bulgarie.

france24fr.title: France : Emmanuel Macron critique la “drôle d’arrogance” de Marine Le Pen
france24fr.description: À Bruxelles, les négociations sur le prochain budget de l'Union européenne se heurtent aux divisions des Vingt-Sept. La présidentielle française de 2027 s'est aussi invitée dans les discussions : Marine Le Pen, candidate du Rassemblement national, a accusé le président de s'adonner à de "basses manoeuvres politiciennes" en voulant verrouiller le budget européen avant l'élection présidentielle. Le président lui a répondu.

france24fr.title: Budget de l'UE : fin du sommet européen sans accord trouvé
france24fr.description: Les ⁠chefs d'Etat ​et de gouvernement de l'Union européenne ne ​se réuniront pas comme prévu vendredi pour la seconde journée de leur sommet à Bruxelles, a ‌annoncé jeudi soir le ⁠chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz, déclarant qu'ils s'évertueraient à ‌trouver d'ici la fin de l'année un ⁠accord sur le budget du bloc.

france24fr.title: La CAN 2025 revient au Sénégal, navires russes ciblés en Libye, incendie au Caire : l'hebdo Afrique
Japon : de la révolte étudiante à la lutte armée, sur les traces de l'Armée rouge
france24fr.description: À la fin des années 1960, la contestation gagne les universités japonaises. Une fraction de l'extrême gauche choisit la lutte armée. En 1972, deux événements marquent cette bascule : le siège du chalet Asama, retransmis en direct à la télévision japonaise, et l'attentat de l'aéroport de Lod, près de Tel-Aviv. Plus de cinquante ans après les faits, France 24 a rencontré deux anciens militants.

france24fr.title: Cueillir des plantes sauvages, le nouveau passe-temps des jeunes
france24fr.description: Pour comprendre pourquoi la cueillette redevient tendance, le média européen ENTR est parti à la rencontre de Beatrice Bisaglia, une passionnée de plantes sauvages qui partage ses connaissances sur Instagram. Au-delà du phénomène sur les réseaux sociaux, le retour de la cueillette en dit long sur les évolutions de notre société et sur une partie de la jeunesse.

france24fr.title: La France entre en récession, le PIB continue de reculer
france24fr.description: Le produit intérieur brut a reculé de 0,2 % au troisième trimestre 2026, annonce l'Insee vendredi. Avec deux trimestres négatifs consécutifs, le pays est dans une période de récession, selon l'institut statistique.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : la fin de l'Eldorado pour les étrangers
france24fr.description: Longtemps terre d'accueil pour ceux qui fuyaient les conflits et les persécutions, l'Afrique du Sud est devenue un pays de plus en plus hostile aux étrangers. Sur fond de chômage et de précarité, les mouvements anti-immigration gagnent du terrain. Des réfugiés sont chassés de leurs logements, des commerces sont vandalisés et des migrants sont menacés jusque dans les hôpitaux et les universités. Reportage de notre correspondante Caroline Dumay.

france24fr.title: PFAS dans les aliments : une ONG dénonce des "failles" réglementaires
france24fr.description: Les limites réglementaires qui fixent les seuils de "polluants éternels" (PFAS) autorisés dans les aliments présentent des "failles" et ne "garantissent pas une protection suffisante" des consommateurs, déplore Générations Futures dans un rapport publié jeudi.

france24fr.title: Sandrine Bonnaire, l'art de rester libre
france24fr.description: Figure libre et singulière du cinéma français, Sandrine Bonnaire traverse les époques sans jamais perdre son franc-parler. Révélée par Maurice Pialat, récompensée par deux César, elle revient aujourd'hui dans "Le Lièvre", de Gonzague Legout. Elle y incarne une mère au passé douloureux. Rencontre avec une actrice et une femme engagée.

france24fr.title: Sur Netflix Inde, une série pakistanaise interdit par le gouvernement Modi
france24fr.description: À la une de la presse ce vendredi 27 novembre : des Brésiliens envoyés par Moscou sur le front en Ukraine, les élections municipales à Taïpei sous pression chinoise, une série pakistanaise bannie en Inde, et des cartes de vœux un peu spéciales.

france24fr.title: Maroc : retour sur le succès du jardin Majorelle à Marrakech
france24fr.description: Ouvert au public en 1947, le Jardin Majorelle, connu pour son bleu intense, est sauvé par Pierre Berger et Yves Saint-Laurent dans les années 1980 après une période difficile. Situé dans celle qu'on surnomme la Perle du Sud, ce patrimoine vivant continue de faire rayonner la ville, un des sites culturels et touristiques les plus visités du Maroc.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Espagne : dernier jour de campagne
france24fr.description: Les électeurs espagnols se ⁠rendent aux urnes dimanche ​pour renouveler la quasi-totalité des membres des Cortes Generales, le Parlement du pays, après ​la décision prise début octobre par le président du gouvernement Pedro Sanchez, en poste depuis huit ans, de convoquer des élections anticipées.

phys-org.title: Roller-coaster flight reveals hidden electricity in clouds
phys-org.description: Measuring the electric charge in widespread, dull gray clouds could help scientists better understand droplets within them, a new study suggests.

phys-org.title: Remote sensing maps rubber yields on Hainan Island
phys-org.description: A new study has developed a method to estimate rubber yields across Hainan Island, one of China's main natural rubber–producing regions. Using high-resolution remote sensing data, meteorological data and a limited set of field measurements, the team mapped annual dry rubber yields from 2021 to 2025.

phys-org.title: A small galaxy's giant dark matter core challenges the standard cosmological model
phys-org.description: New findings show that a nearby dwarf galaxy, UGCA 320, may challenge some predictions of the widely accepted cosmological model of the universe. By combining observations from the MUSE instrument with radio measurements from the MeerKAT telescope, astronomers have found that it hosts an unusually large dark matter core. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Nov. 11.

phys-org.title: Measuring surprise in online attention
phys-org.description: The difference between attention and surprise matters when public-interest forecasts guide media planning or decisions about the capacity needed to handle traffic. The paper, presented at the IEEE Technology and Engineering Management Society Conference (TEMSCON LATAM) in Quito, Ecuador, in June 2026, provides a common statistical approach for following changes in attention and forecast errors separately.

phys-org.title: Winner takes it all? Study highlights rise of zero-sum politics
phys-org.description: A growing tendency to view politics as a battle in which one group can only succeed at another's expense could be slowing economic growth and eroding support for Western democracies, according to new research by King's College London academics.

phys-org.title: Cosmology technique inspires better characterization of ocean swirls and waves
phys-org.description: A new study from Caltech uses a mathematical framework borrowed from cosmology to analyze ocean data and characterize individual flow features in the churning chaos. With the technique, the researchers are able to measure and characterize features in maps of the ocean surface, allowing them to differentiate ocean flows that otherwise look identical when evaluated with standard analysis tools.

phys-org.title: New soil test could help farmers avoid costly crop damage
phys-org.description: Herbicides are essential for controlling weeds, but chemicals remaining in the soil after application can damage crops planted in subsequent seasons, particularly during dry conditions.

phys-org.title: Drones offer a new view of wildlife health. But what are they missing?
phys-org.description: Drones are transforming how scientists study wildlife, allowing researchers to photograph and measure animals in their natural environments, monitor larger populations and collect observations with less disturbance. While a photograph can reveal changes in an animal's size and shape, it cannot confidently tell researchers what those changes mean for its health.

phys-org.title: Bushfire disaster ignites citizen science tourism
phys-org.description: The devastating Black Summer wildfires on Kangaroo Island accelerated interest in citizen science tourism—a movement gaining momentum as climate-related disasters place unprecedented pressure on native species and landscapes.

phys-org.title: Nonlinear optical lattice boosts spatial coherence by concentrating light in a single mode
phys-org.description: Light waves can have varying degrees of coherence, which means that the consistency of the relationship between their phases across space or time can differ. Reliable methods to enhance the coherence of light could pave the way for the development of high-quality lasers and scientific instruments.

phys-org.title: Study finds lasting changes in daily mobility patterns across Latin America after COVID-19
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Liverpool have used anonymized Facebook mobility data to explore how everyday movement patterns changed across Latin American countries in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.

phys-org.title: What are the odds of a volcano erupting through a salt lake?
phys-org.description: An experimental study of what happens when volcanoes erupt through salt lakes is rewriting the genesis story on the formation of some iron ore and rare earth deposits. The Australian National University (ANU) research looks beyond common assumptions, reconciling decades of research. The findings indicate that the various proposed mineral formation routes, or genesis pathways, are not necessarily mutually exclusive.

phys-org.title: Decoding how fish adapt to varying salt concentrations
phys-org.description: Freshwater and seawater fishes face different challenges in maintaining the balance of salts and water in their bodies. To survive these changing conditions, they rely on specialized transport proteins in organs like the kidneys and intestine to regulate electrolyte transport. However, important questions regarding the molecular mechanisms that support salt transport and acclimatization to different environmental salinities persist.

phys-org.title: Beeswax and pine link crocodile mummies made centuries apart at one Egyptian site
phys-org.description: In a practice spanning centuries, ancient Egyptians mummified thousands of crocodiles they associated with Sobek, a god linked to the Nile, fertility and royal power. In one unique example, embalmers from the middle of the 1st millennium BC at Kom Ombo in southern Egypt mounted more than 25 hatchlings on reeds along the back and neck of a crocodile nearly 4 meters (13 feet) long. The arrangement may echo the way young crocodiles ride on their mother's back.

phys-org.title: Bacterial colonies turn themselves inside out when oxygen is scarce
phys-org.description: Bacteria can protect themselves from external threats by forming colonies. The physical principles that govern the structure of such colonies, and in particular their structural transformations, are poorly understood.

phys-org.title: New atlas unites nearly 3,500 laser surveys to map forests across 56 countries
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers led by the University of Bristol in the U.K. has unveiled the Global Canopy Atlas—the largest integrated collection of high-resolution 3D maps of forests, woodlands and savannas ever assembled.

phys-org.title: Digital access to early music

Developed specifically for the Renaissance lute, this rich notational tradition preserves dances, songs and other musical works that were immensely popular some 500 years ago. phys-org.title: Why molecular cage catalysts show enormous differences in performance
phys-org.description: Chemistry researchers have developed a new way to identify and understand highly effective artificial enzyme-like catalysts using powerful "molecular cages" that mimic the behavior of nature's enzymes. These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions. The cages showed enormous differences in performance, with the best catalysts more than 10,000 times more active than the least effective ones.

undark.title: For Sale: Custom Space Program, Ready to Launch
undark.description: Countries that couldn’t previously afford their own national program can now purchase a space-program-in-a-box through private companies, allowing them to access aerial surveillance capabilities and provide more resilient communication and GPS services. What does the shift mean for geopolitics?

undark.title: Could a Blow to the Head Appear in the Gut?
undark.description: Concussions and other head trauma may leave detectable fingerprints in the gut microbiome. Some experts hope such markers could help diagnose and treat brain injuries, which currently rely on symptom-based assessments. But research is still nascent and questions remain.

undark.title: Review: The Pernicious Fallout From the Early Atomic Testing Era
undark.description: In “Frenchman Flat: The Rise and Fall of Atomic Bombs,” Jon Else chronicles the early days of atomic weapons testing in postwar Nevada and the impact of moving clouds of residual radioactivity, a troubling reminder that the pernicious effects of nuclear weapons aren’t limited to their use in wartime.

undark.title: The Strange History of Future Sea Level Rise
undark.description: Sea level projections primarily rely on a satellite record that spans roughly the length of a typical mortgage. Some scientists, though, think the deep past may offer clues modern predictive models don’t honor. Could studying ancient ice sheets help forecast future sea level rise?

undark.title: Understanding Pregnancy’s Role in Ebola
undark.description: Opinion | Pregnant women are particularly susceptible to Ebola and contribute to its spread, yet little research has been done into the immune system’s responses to Ebola during pregnancy. Handling future outbreaks will require understanding the deep biological connections between pregnancy and viral infections.

undark.title: Book Review: The Man Who Gave Animals Their Voice
undark.description: Primatologist Frans De Waal’s memoir “Minds I’ve Met: From Denying to Embracing the Inner Lives of Animals,” reveals how his work has helped to shatter the imaginary wall that science once erected between humans and other animals and radically revised the way we think and speak about other creatures.

undark.title: Interview: How the Cold War Brain Drain Upended Soviet Science
undark.description: Historian of science Elena Aronova, one of many Russian researchers who left the Soviet Union after the Cold War, discusses the fraying of the nation’s massive scientific infrastructure and how a superpower responsible for Sputnik could could end with research laboratories struggling to keep the lights on.

undark.title: From the Editor: The Weight of Uncertainty
undark.description: In search of a vanished ice sheet — and clues to better answer a pivotal question: How far will global sea level rise? Also in this issue: A brain-gut connection may offer insight into concussion treatment and a look at how ready-made space programs could alter geopolitics.

undark.title: Aftershock: Untangling the Risks of Electroconvulsive Therapy
undark.description: Psychiatrists and other experts, backed by studies, maintain that ECT is safe and effective for severe psychiatric conditions including depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. But some ECT patients report lasting cognitive harm and say they weren’t adequately warned of potential side effects.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

public-dom.title: Bickering Buildings: A Dialogue Between the Churches of Athens in 1854
public-dom.description: The churches of Athens had much to say in 1854, when an anonymous author staged a squabble between them in newsprint. public-dom.description: Surprisingly mellow illustrations of war and myth from a book of advice for young noblemen.

public-dom.title: Soldiers of Misfortune: The Drawings of Urs Graf the Elder
public-dom.description: A mercenary and miscreant, the Swiss Renaissance artist Urs Graf lived the violence and vice he summoned on his drafting table. public-dom.description: When the Bristol Channel flooded in 1607, it was not just one of the worst natural disasters in British history, it was also a sign, for many, that they had strayed from the path of God. Erik Crnkovich examines the overlap of miraculous weather and the early modern printing industry, which cultivated a thirst for all things occult, exotic, and odd.

public-dom.title: “Men with Queer Nerves”: The Jumping Frenchmen of Maine
public-dom.description: In the late nineteenth century, visitors to Maine observed something strange: French-Canadian lumberjacks who, at the slightest stimulus, seemed to jump, strike out with their limbs, or mimic languages they could not speak. Ross Bullen introduces us to these so-called “Jumping Frenchmen” and to their greatest investigator, George M. Beard, who saw a link in their behavior between religious frenzy and neurasthenia.

public-dom.title: Rudolf Kalvach’s Wiener Werkstätte Postcards (1907)

public-dom.title: The Alchemical Transformations of the Mutus Liber (1677)

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

eurozine.title: Obstinacy

Som enskild människa måste man leva igenom även mycket dåliga tider. Strategierna kan vara många. Kanske måste, menar Sennett, socialismen sätta det sociala tillbaka på agendan, för att förbereda sig för en tid efter Trump.

proj-syn.title: The Future of the Global Disability Agenda
proj-syn.description: The once-reasonable assumption that integrating disabled people into the existing multilateral order would help them benefit from the results being delivered no longer holds. Achieving better outcomes requires learning from disability movements about how to put diversity, access, care, and participation at the center of the agenda.

proj-syn.title: Can the AI Mineral Rush Advance a Just Green Transition?
proj-syn.description: The scramble to secure huge amounts of copper, aluminum, lithium, cobalt, and other minerals for AI infrastructure risks undoing the progress made, as part of the green transition, toward more responsible mining practices. But it could also be an opportunity to support sustainable development in producer countries.

proj-syn.title: The Evolving Terrain of the Global AI Transformation
proj-syn.description: The race to build ever more powerful AI models is heating up, but so far there is little evidence of the promised productivity surge. Whether that changes will depend on how quickly employers adopt AI and whether governments can encourage its use while managing the risks of job losses and public backlash.

proj-syn.title: How Congress Can Give Americans What They Want
proj-syn.description: American households are footing the bill for President Donald Trump’s tariffs and war in Iran through higher prices and borrowing costs. Congress has the power to stop this by reclaiming its authority over tariff policy and the use of military force, and by requiring a public accounting of the costs of future wars.

proj-syn.title: The Revolt Against Oligarchy
proj-syn.description: The extraordinary power wielded by today’s billionaires is a threat to democracy and the planet. Encouragingly, people around the world, frustrated by a lack of affordability and worsening job prospects, are beginning to discover just how much political power they can wield.

proj-syn.title: Who Can Speak for Europe in Peace Talks with Russia?
proj-syn.description: The European Union's inability to find one person to represent it in such negotiations reflects a structural failure, not a shortage of skilled personnel. That is why the EU should step aside and delegate the selection of an envoy to the United Kingdom, France, and Germany.

proj-syn.title: The Fossil-Fuel Endgame Doesn’t Require a COP Consensus
proj-syn.description: Despite the failure of this year's United Nations climate talks, there is no doubt that phasing out fossil fuels is the right goal. The only question is whether a coalition of the willing can use policy to push markets toward a faster, fairer, and smoother transition than the traditional COP process can deliver.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls America’s AI Chokepoint?
proj-syn.description: The saga of Jensen Huang's ouster and sudden return as Nvidia's chief executive has exposed a paradox at the heart of American technological hegemony. While Nvidia's AI chips give the United States leverage over China, the geopolitical power that Nvidia makes possible gives it leverage over the US.

proj-syn.title: Where Development Cooperation Still Lives
proj-syn.description: By helping developing economies build the capacity and infrastructure trade requires, the World Trade Organization's Aid for Trade initiative has contributed to a significant increase in these countries' share of global exports over the past 20 years. But the trade landscape is changing fast, and Aid for Trade must adapt.

proj-syn.title: Nvidia’s Liability Problem Isn’t Going Away
proj-syn.description: Given previous suspicions about Nvidia's engagement with China, one wonders if Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affairs are just a cover-up for more consequential violations and misrepresentations. Whatever the case, the problem is not limited to Huang; with his reinstatement as CEO, it involves the company's entire board.

proj-syn.title: Mapping Strategic Supply-Chain Risk
proj-syn.description: If there is a premium to be paid for resilient supply chains, who will foot the bill? The answer can be found through a three-stage approach of identifying current vulnerabilities, letting markets and public tenders price them, and then having national-security authorities intervene only where market pricing fails.

proj-syn.title: Holiday 2026 Reading List
proj-syn.description: In the bi-weekly PS Book Recommendations newsletter—available for free to all registered PS readers—we highlight insightful, informative, or otherwise compelling books, written or recommended by PS contributors. Here, we present a selection of recent works by PS contributors that are worth adding to your holiday shopping list (and your bookshelf).

proj-syn.title: The Summit of Self-Promotion
proj-syn.description: Despite claiming that world history was made in Shenzhen with the US–Russia–China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, the trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin was about optics, not substance. One of the many important problems they failed to address was China’s export-led growth.

proj-syn.title: Why Nvidia Couldn’t Quit Jensen Huang
proj-syn.description: Developing AI requires tremendous coordination across firms and sectors, from the AI labs themselves to energy and computing infrastructure, as well as long-term vision and patience. Whereas much of this coordination and planning is led by the government in China, in the US, it has been driven largely by one CEO.

proj-syn.title: Chips Too Big to Fail
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia to keep the stock market high, to feed a possible productivity surge, and to advance a US foreign policy built on reconciliation with China. But will Americans continue to believe in the AI miracle and this new version of Chimerica?

proj-syn.title: Amplifying the Voice of Human Limits
proj-syn.description: Tech leaders like Elon Musk have embraced Prometheus as a symbol of creation, conquest, and discovery. But the Promethean impulse must be balanced by the “Orphic” tradition’s respect for and contemplation of nature’s mystery.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of South Korea’s Semiconductor Boom
proj-syn.description: The AI boom has driven South Korea’s economic growth well above expectations, thanks to soaring demand for advanced semiconductors. But AI’s transformative potential does not guarantee that the current investment frenzy will continue, leaving the economy vulnerable to a downturn.

proj-syn.title: Is a Financial-Market Reckoning Imminent?
proj-syn.description: After a year of unprecedented AI investment, increasingly financed by debt in opaque private markets, growing unease about the industry’s future is reflected in sharp declines in the NASDAQ index and the S&P 500. But the stock market’s dependence on a handful of highly leveraged companies—and even a single CEO—is hardly the only source of global financial risk. Amid mounting fears, we asked PS contributors what to expect from financial markets in the year ahead.
